edges.description: Without IKK2, IkappaB is not phosphorylated and NF-kappaB is not released for nuclear translocation.
NF-kappaB is required to transduce activation signals from antigen, pattern-recognition, and cytokine receptors.
Failed B-cell activation and germinal-center reactions produce hypogammaglobulinemia.
In the most severe cases immunoglobulin is absent.
Failure of lymphocyte activation and differentiation produces a combined humoral and cellular immunodeficiency.
The combined immunodeficiency manifests as severe, recurrent, early-onset infections.
The organism-level outcome is a clinical combined immunodeficiency.
Impaired innate/adaptive immunity confers susceptibility to mycobacteria, including vaccine-strain BCG.
Susceptibility extends to fungal infection, including mucocutaneous candidiasis.
Early-onset severe infection is usually accompanied by failure to thrive.
The mouse null is embryonic-lethal and cannot recapitulate the viable human immunodeficiency.
edges.limitations: Embryonic lethality precludes study of the immune phenotype in the complete mouse knockout, a species-divergence limitation.

nodes.description: Biallelic IKBKB loss-of-function variants abolish expression of IKK2 (IKKbeta), the catalytic kinase of the IKK complex that phosphorylates IkappaB to trigger canonical NF-kappaB activation.

Constitutive Ikbkb (Ikk2) knockout is embryonic-lethal in mice, so the mouse null does not model the viable human combined immunodeficiency; the human phenotype indicates a more restricted role of IKK2-NF-kappaB signaling in humans than the mouse predicts.

evidence.snippet: Immunoglobulin replacement was variable between patients and generally continued between 3- and 12-months post-HSCT.

nodes.description: Because canonical NF-kappaB cannot be activated, T cells, B cells, and innate immune cells fail to respond to receptor stimulation. Despite normal development and counts, circulating T and B cells remain almost exclusively naive and cannot mature into memory/effector subsets; regulatory T cells and gamma-delta T cells are absent.
